# Condensation (data analysis and visulaization)¶

This tutorial demonstrates how to visualize the selected AE spectrum and process the entire dataset for use in unsupervised machine learning. The unsupervised learning will then classify the dataset based on two different vapor qualities. For this tutorial you will need to download and unzip data and keep in the same working directory. More information about the dataset is available in the README file.
Read a csv from a folder (Gnpfh10_0_Gw25_x0_60_dirVD_p18_9/AE/inlet) in the dataset to visulize the AE hits and Spectrum

#Link the folder to this ipynb
%cd Gnpfh10_0_Gw25_x0_60_dirVD_p18_9/AE/inlet

import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# Read the CSV file into a DataFrame for visualization

df = pd.read_csv("inlet_15_1_1000_59301378.csv", skiprows=12)
plt.figure(figsize=(6, 3))
plt.plot(df.iloc[:, 0])
plt.xlabel("Time")
plt.ylabel("AE hits")
plt.grid(True)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from scipy.fftpack import fft

# Read data, skipping first 12 rows as those are description of the file
df = pd.read_csv("inlet_15_1_1000_59301378.csv", skiprows=12)

# Extract first column as 1D numpy array
waveform = df.iloc[:, 0].values

ae_fs = 1e6  # Sampling frequency in Hz
N = len(waveform)

# Compute FFT magnitude (first half)
P = np.abs(fft(waveform))[:N//2]

# Convert magnitude to decibels (add small epsilon to avoid log(0))
P_db = 10 * np.log10(P + np.finfo(np.float32).eps)

# Normalize (zero mean, unit std)
P_norm = (P_db - np.mean(P_db)) / np.std(P_db)

# Frequency axis (in kHz)
freqs = np.linspace(0, ae_fs/2, num=N//2) / 1000

# Plot
plt.figure(figsize=(6, 3))
plt.plot(freqs, P_norm)
#plt.title("Normalized FFT Spectrum of First Column")
plt.xlabel("Frequency (kHz)")
plt.ylabel("FFT Power (dB)")
plt.grid(True)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
Read data form x0=0.60, visualize selected AE Spectrum and Process the whole dataset to be used in unsupervised machine learning

#Link the folder to this ipynb
%cd ../../../Gnpfh10_0_Gw25_x0_60_dirVD_p18_9/AE/inlet

import pandas as pd
import glob
import os

# Path to the directory containing the CSV files
folder_path = "."

# Get list of all CSV files in the folder
csv_files = glob.glob(os.path.join(folder_path, "*.csv"))

# List to store individual DataFrames
dfs = []

# Read each CSV, skip 12 rows, and append to list
for file in csv_files:
    df = pd.read_csv(file, skiprows=12)
    dfs.append(df)

# Concatenate all DataFrames column-wise (axis=1)
combined_df = pd.concat(dfs, axis=1)

# Show the shape of the final DataFrame
print("Combined DataFrame shape:", combined_df.shape)

df=combined_df

import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np
from scipy.fftpack import fft

# Sampling frequency (Hz)
ae_fs = 1e6  

# Function to compute normalized FFT
def compute_normalized_fft(signal, fs):
    N = len(signal)
    P = np.abs(fft(signal))[:N//2]
    P_db = 10 * np.log10(P + np.finfo(np.float32).eps)  # Avoid log(0)
    P_norm = (P_db - np.mean(P_db)) / np.std(P_db)
    freqs = np.linspace(0, fs/2, num=N//2) / 1000  # in kHz
    return freqs, P_norm

# Plot FFTs for every 100th column
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 6))

for col_index in range(99, df.shape[1], 100):
    signal = df.iloc[:, col_index].values
    freqs, P_norm = compute_normalized_fft(signal, ae_fs)
    plt.plot(freqs, P_norm, label=f'Col {col_index+1}')

#plt.title("Normalized FFT of Every 100th Column")
plt.xlabel("Frequency (kHz)")
plt.ylabel("FFT Power (dB)")
plt.legend(loc="upper right", fontsize="small", ncol=2)
plt.grid(True)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()


# List to store P_norm arrays
pnorm_list = []

# Corresponding column labels
column_labels = []

# Loop through every 100th column
for col_index in range(99, df.shape[1], 1):
    signal = df.iloc[:, col_index].values
    freqs, P_norm = compute_normalized_fft(signal, ae_fs)
    pnorm_list.append(P_norm)
    column_labels.append(f'Col_{col_index+1}')

# Convert list of arrays to DataFrame (transpose so each column is one FFT result)
pnorm_df0= pd.DataFrame(np.array(pnorm_list).T, columns=column_labels)

# Optional: show the shape of the FFT result DataFrame
print("FFT result DataFrame shape:", pnorm_df0.shape)
pnorm_df0.to_csv("../../../df0.csv", index=False)

import os
import pandas as pd
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
from sklearn.cluster import KMeans
from sklearn.decomposition import PCA
from sklearn.metrics import adjusted_rand_score
import umap.umap_ as umap
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

os.chdir('../../../')

# Replace 'filename.csv' with your actual file name or path
df0 = pd.read_csv("df0.csv")
df1 = pd.read_csv("df1.csv")
df1 = df1.dropna(axis=1)
df0 = df0.dropna(axis=1)

df0 = df0.T
df1 = df1.T

df0['c'] = 0
df1['c'] = 1

# Assuming df0 and df1 are preloaded DataFrames with same columns
df_combined = pd.concat([df0, df1], ignore_index=True)

# Separate features (all but last column) and true labels (last column)
X = df_combined.iloc[:, :-1]
y_true = df_combined.iloc[:, -1].values

# PCA reduction to 25 components
pca = PCA(n_components=25)
X_pca = pca.fit_transform(X)

# UMAP reduction to 4 components
umap_model = umap.UMAP(n_components=4, min_dist=0)
X_umap = umap_model.fit_transform(X_pca)

# KMeans clustering with 2 clusters
kmeans = KMeans(n_clusters=2, random_state=0, n_init="auto")
y_pred = kmeans.fit_predict(X_umap)

# Compute Adjusted Rand Score comparing true and predicted labels
ars = adjusted_rand_score(y_true, y_pred)
print(f"Adjusted Rand Score : {ars:.4f}")

# Optional: Plot UMAP result colored by predicted cluster
plt.scatter(X_umap[:, 0], X_umap[:, 1], c=y_pred, s=10)
#plt.title("UMAP projection colored by KMeans clusters")
plt.xlabel("UMAP Dimension 1")
plt.ylabel("UMAP Dimension 2")
#plt.colorbar(label='Cluster')
plt.show()
